checks.claim: 23 DOF columns = 25 model coordinates minus knee_angle_r_beta and knee_angle_l_beta
evidence: Independent ElementTree parse of ta22/07 dynamics_model.osim: 25 coordinates in the adapter's H25 order. Two CoordinateCouplerConstraints (patellofemoral_knee_angle_<s>_con) are enforced, with knee_angle_<s>_beta = 1 x knee_angle_<s> + 0.

Under the alternative (first 23 coordinates), dof10 would be knee_angle_r_beta and equal dof09. On the seeded trials, max |dof10 - dof09| = 1.26 rad (fa16/subject_5 Gait_6) and 1.76 rad (ta21/s8 mini_SI_28), so that hypothesis is refuted.
The adapter's check_model refuses any model whose coordinates, couplers, ground_pelvis transform or gravity differ, so H23 is re-checked per participant.

checks.claim: Hip flexion, knee flexion and ankle dorsiflexion are positive in the source (+1), and so is their generalized force
evidence: Independent rotation-only FK. Offset frames use body-fixed XYZ; joints compose body-fixed. Walker-knee splines are included. A +0.2 rad step gives these world rotation vectors: pelvis_tilt (0,0,+0.2); hip_flexion_r/l (0,0,+0.2), counterclockwise about +z (right), i.e. thigh forward; knee_angle_r/l z = -0.202, clockwise, i.e. shank back = flexion; ankle_angle_r/l z = +0.196, toes up = dorsiflexion. The knee range is 0 to 2.0944 rad. This is the Rajagopal walker knee (flexion +), not gait2392 (flexion -), so +1 is right here.

Seeded data (raw-force events, review only), median per stride. Tan walking ta22/05 fpa: knee peak 1.11-1.15 rad at 68-70 % of the stride, after toe-off (58-61 %) in 100 % of strides. Ankle minimum -0.41 to -0.49 rad within 15 % of toe-off in 100 % of strides. Stance ankle moment minimum -1.34 to -1.38 N*m/kg (plantarflexor, negative under rule B) in 100 %. Hip moment -0.19 to -0.27 (extensor) early and +0.37 to +0.43 (flexor) late in stance.

Tan running ta21/s8 mini_SI_28: knee peak 1.41-1.43 rad at 68-69 % (toe-off 35 %). Ankle minimum at 39-40 %. Stance ankle moment minimum -3.03 N*m/kg. Hip moment -0.80 to -0.92 early and +0.26 to +0.50 late.
tau is the generalized force conjugate to each coordinate (nimblephysics FramePass.tau), so it is positive in the coordinate's named direction; the data above agree.

checks.claim: pelvis_tilt is ground-relative (obliquity when facing -z); pitch = asin(up component of the pelvis anterior axis) from the full body-fixed Rz(tilt) Rx(list) Ry(rotation); rule-B sign
checks.result: pass (rotation order supported by data; OpenSim documentation not re-fetched)
evidence: ground_pelvis in the .osim: rotation1 pelvis_tilt about (0,0,1), rotation2 pelvis_list about (1,0,0), rotation3 pelvis_rotation about (0,1,0); all linear 1 0; both offset frames unrotated. The .osim itself does not state the composition order.

Data test of the order, using the dominant harmonic per stride (1 = stride frequency, typical of obliquity; 2 = step frequency, typical of pitch). ta21/s8, facing yaw 86 deg: dof00 (tilt) is at stride frequency in 13 of 13 strides, so it behaves as obliquity. Derived roll is at stride frequency in 100 % of strides under body-fixed composition, against 23 % under space-fixed. ta22/05, facing +x: dof01 (list) is at stride frequency in 100 %. Body-fixed is supported; space-fixed is not.
Adapter pelvis_anterior_axis checked by hand: Rz(t) Rx(l) Ry(r) e_x = (ct cr - st sl sr, st cr + ct sl sr, -cl sr), which matches the code.

Sign: the anterior axis rising (front up) gives positive pitch. By rule B, counterclockwise about +z is front up, i.e. posterior tilt positive and anterior tilt negative. FK pelvis_tilt +0.2 about +z gives +0.2 pitch at zero yaw. Seeded medians: running -0.10 rad (anterior), walking +0.12 rad. Zero offsets are not assessed (already listed as not checked in the mapping record).

checks.claim: Walking direction from stance CoP (treadmill) or COM travel (overground), within 45 deg of facing; z' = x' x y' is the person's right
evidence: Cross product: (0,0,-1) x (0,1,0) = (1,0,0), so facing -z puts the right side at world +x. (1,0,0) x (0,1,0) = (0,0,1). The adapter's frame_basis and the corrected test agree.

Data laterality, independent of the CoP axis (x' taken from the pelvis facing). The mean stance CoP projected on z' is larger for the right foot than for the left: fa16/subject_5 0.261 vs 0.126 m; ta21/s8 0.292 vs 0.255 m. Right is to the right.

ta21/s8: within-stance CoP principal axis 3.7 deg from facing. Note: on a treadmill the lab-frame CoP moves backward within stance (mean -0.38 m along the forward axis). The CoP supplies only the axis; the sense comes from facing. The code does exactly this. 'CoP progression' in the handoff summary means the axis only.
Overground fa16/subject_5 Gait_6: facing yaw 2 deg (world +x), consistent with the mapping record.

checks.claim: GRF is the force on the foot in the world frame, mapped to the rule-B frame
evidence: Vertical force is positive in stance (ground on person, +y up; model gravity 0 -9.80665 0).

Recorded force, review only, ta22/05 fpa, 18 stances per leg: anterior force is -67 to -72 N in the first 30 % of stance (braking) and +79 to +80 N in the last 30 % (propulsion). Outward lateral force is -48 to -51 N for both legs (medial), negative in 100 % of stances, as expected. Running ta21/s8 anterior is likewise -67/-74 then +100/+91 N. Running outward lateral force is small and positive for both legs (+5 to +7 N, narrow base). This is not a laterality signal, because CoP placement confirms laterality; it is left not checked.

findings.severity: blocking for this pilot's stated purpose (not a correctness or safety error: with the current table nothing can be published)
findings.finding: missing_grf_reason is a per-frame flag, not per-foot. The adapter blanks both feet's force on every flagged frame and then requires every frame of a stride to be finite (stride_pairs, heel_strikes). On real data this removes stance force that was recorded. ta21/s8 mini_SI_28: footContactDetectedButNoForce covers flight frames and 335 single-stance frames above 50 N; missingBlip covers whole stances. ta22/05 fpa: 75 % of frames flagged, including stances of 700 N or more. The adapter's own stride_pairs finds 0 strides in 143 of 143 ta21/s3 trials and in all 5 fa16/subject_0 trials (61 of 2,587 frames clean). ta22/07 is fine: 1,058 strides in 41 of 48 trials. So in the pilot, every TA21 and FA16 trial falls back to 100-frame blocks with no detector task, and no plate-timing tests run.
findings.consequence: The pilot's expected outcome ('records detector verdicts per channel, the data evidence the proposed entries need') and the proposed entries' evidence_basis ('HIST-06 pilot plate-timing evidence', 'pilot push-off evidence') can be met only for TA22. FA16 and TA21 would rest on the model definition alone.
options_for_worker: Agent-level fix: take stride events (unit boundaries only) from the recorded vertical force regardless of the frame flag, keep the standardized GRF empty on flagged frames, and pass the evidence GRF NaN-masked (the detector handles NaN). Add a synthetic fixture with flight-phase and whole-stance flags, then re-plan as v1r4.
Or re-scope explicitly: state in the pilot plan and the proposed entries that FA16 and TA21 sign evidence is the model definition (FK) only, and launch v1r3 as a frame/task/row/undo test.
findings.for_coordinator: José's 2026-11-02 rule says to keep recorded values unless they are blatant errors. Blanking recorded plate force on frames flagged for the other foot or for a blip may conflict with that rule. It also excludes data: 98 % of fa16/subject_0 frames, 54 % of ta21/s3 and 15 % of ta22/07. Please decide whether this is an agent-level 'unavailable measurement' choice or a José-level exclusion before the full run. The source values and the flag stay in the HIST-05 files, so it is reversible.

findings.severity: blocking until the coordinator confirms (scientific: zero-filled unavailable values)
findings.finding: The diff also removed 'CoP empty where that foot's vertical force is not positive'. That rule is not flag-based: the CoP of an unloaded foot is undefined. In the source it is stored as an exact (0,0,0) placeholder, not NaN. ta21/s3 right foot: 172,234 of 172,608 unloaded frames have CoP exactly (0,0,0), and none is NaN. ta22/07 both feet: 58,734 of 67,220. fa16/subject_0: 242 of 243. Loaded frames (above 50 N): 0 such frames in fa16/subject_0 and ta22/07. With decf23a3..., cop_anterior/vertical/lateral_*_m will read 0 m (the world origin) on every swing and flight frame. Users would read that as a measured position. AGENTS.md and docs/reference: 'Unavailable signals stay missing. Zero-filled missing features can create false evidence that a signal was measured.' The detector's resampled CoP evidence also mixes these zeros into stride edges.
findings.why_not_covered_by_the_ruling: The ruling 'recorded zeros stay zero' fits force: a zero force on an unloaded foot is a measurement. A (0,0,0) CoP on the same frame is not a recorded position. The ruling as written ('empty only where the source is NaN') covers it literally, but it was made about the flag.
findings.fix_proposed: One line in grf_world: c = where((f[:, 1] > 0)[:, None], c, nan), using the recorded force with no flag involved. Restore 'empty where that foot's recorded vertical force is not positive' in the docstring and in the mapping record row for calcn_*_cop. Give the synthetic fixture a (0,0,0) CoP on unloaded frames, with expectations: NaN where unloaded, recorded CoP where loaded (including flagged frames). Then re-plan as v1r5 and dry-run.
findings.for_coordinator: Confirm this narrowing of the F1 ruling (CoP undefined at zero load), or explicitly accept zero CoP on unloaded frames with a documented note. Reversible either way: the source values stay in the HIST-05 files.

findings.finding: Adapter module docstring item 4 still says strides use 'all frames with measured GRF'. It should say recorded vertical force, flags ignored.

checks.claim: Frame-by-frame value spot check against the source
checks.result: pass (segment identity not checkable: no published inputs)
evidence: Seed 20261104 (random.Random over each participant's mapped trial indices) drew fa16/subject_0 trial 1 (STS_1, 633 frames), ta21/s3 trial 82 (nike_SI_24, 2000 frames) and ta22/07 trial 23 (step_width, 2000 frames). Added as a fixed, not random, case: fa16/subject_0 trial 0 (Gait_7), the only Falisse locomotion trial. Both reference sides and the ipsi/contra roles were checked per frame.
Passed 52/52 in each locomotion trial and 40/40 in STS_1:
- source frame order;
- missing_grf_reason carried exactly;
- grf_vertical = recorded Fy on every frame, including flagged ones (flagged loaded right-foot frames kept: 533 in STS_1, 279 in nike_SI_24, 998 in step_width);
- cop_vertical = recorded Cy where that foot's Fy > 0, else empty;
- _BW = N / (recorded entered_mass_kg x 9.80665) (64.8, 57.4, 74.4 kg), and normalization_mass_kg = recorded mass;
- grf_anterior = F.x', grf_lateral = (+1 right, -1 left) x F.z', and the CoP equivalents where loaded, to 1e-6 N and 1e-9 m;
- hip adduction and rotation angle and moment equal the source exactly;
- all held columns empty;
- STS_1: anterior and lateral empty (no forward locomotion).

x' was recovered by least squares from the mapped anterior force. It is unit length and equals my independent re-implementation (CoP principal axis oriented by body-fixed ZXY facing; COM velocity overground) to 0.0000 deg in all three locomotion trials. It also equals the logged direction within the log's 4-decimal rounding. Facing offsets: 3.5, 1.6 and 0.6 deg.

Lateral sign: z' = x' x y. Mean loaded CoP on z' is right foot > left foot in all three: 0.375 vs 0.264 m, 0.649 vs 0.429 m, -0.120 vs -0.285 m. So +z' is the person's right and lateral is outward per leg.

Joint angles and moments: held, so empty in the output. Their source sign and units (rad, N*m generalized force, +1) were verified in round 1 (FK and seeded gait plausibility). Per-kg moments are empty because the moments are held; recorded-mass division is verified on _BW and in the round-2/3 synthetic tests.

The thigh = pelvis + hip, shank = thigh - knee and foot = shank + ankle identities cannot be checked on this output, because no proximal input is published. Coverage remains the synthetic test test_segments_and_velocities_from_published_channels and the pilot's hash-link check (no finding).

checks.claim: Tan running 35 deg offset between walking direction and pelvis facing: diagnosis
checks.result: diagnosed: source kinematic artefact (pelvis segment turned in one recording), not a treadmill/global-frame artefact and not an adapter bug
evidence: The treadmill axis is stable. The within-stance CoP axis yaw spans 87.9-94.0 deg (SD 0.95) over 140 s3 trials, 85.1-93.7 (SD 0.97) in s1 and 88.6-91.7 (SD 0.71) in s8. The global frame and belt direction do not move.

The offset is in one condition only. In s3 every trial with |offset| > 10 deg is one of the 13 nike_SR_24 segments (trials 99-111), median -29.1 deg, maximum -34.7 deg. Every other s3 condition has a median of -3.9 to -0.2 deg. s1 and s8 stay within 5 deg in every trial.

The rest of the body compensates. Across s3 trials, the offset correlates -0.98 with hip_rotation_r - hip_rotation_l (slope -1.6 deg per deg; in nike_SR_24, hip rotation is r +21 to +23 deg and l -22 to -25 deg). It correlates +0.94 with lumbar rotation, which reaches -95 to +91 deg in those segments against -7 to +1 deg elsewhere. The legs and CoP stay aligned with the belt while the fitted pelvis is turned about 30 deg and the lumbar joint absorbs up to 90 deg. That is a kinematic fit failure of that recording, not a turned model (other conditions of the same model are aligned) and not a frame issue.

Effect on the mapping: the walking direction comes from the CoP axis, so the GRF/CoP frame is unaffected. Pelvis pitch is heading-independent but comes from a mis-fitted pelvis. Hip flexion/adduction/rotation in those 13 segments are measured against a turned pelvis: sign unaffected, magnitudes suspect. Published now: hip adduction and rotation (source sign) for those segments carry the artefact.
